entries.title: Exodus 23:2
segments: The majority as to numbers, wealth,and political influence are often wrong.  If in such cases a person would do right, he must not be governed by public opinion, however it may be expressed, but by the law of God.

entries.title: Exodus 23:3
segments: Countenance; unduly favor.  In deciding causes, they were not to favor the rich, the great, or the many; nor were they to be partial towards the poor, but to decide according to evidence, right, and duty.

entries.title: Exodus 23:5
segments:
Lying under his burden; fallen, and not able to rise without help. 
 
  Help with him; assist the owner in getting the beast up.

entries.title: Exodus 23:7
segments:
Far from a false matter; not attempt to support a false accusation. 
 
  Slay thou not; not be accessory to the death of an innocent person. 
 
The laws of Moses, as well as those of Christ, required men to love others as they loved themselves; and, under all circumstances, to do to others as they ought to wish that others should do to them.

entries.title: Exodus 23:8
segments: Gift; a bribe offered to induce a magistrate to favor one in judgment.

entries.title: Exodus 23:9
segments:
A stranger; a foreigner.  They had learned by experience in Egypt the liability of foreigners to be oppressed, and remembered how they felt under oppression. 
 
Might never gives right; and to oppress or wrong any one because he cannot defend himself, or bring to justice the aggressor, is mean, base, and wicked.

entries.title: Exodus 23:11
segments: Let it rest; this was to teach them their dependence on God, and the safety of trusting in him.

entries.title: Exodus 23:12
segments:
Thy work; all worldly business except what was needful in acts of mercy, and for the best discharge of the appropriate duties of the Sabbath. 
 
  May be refreshed; one day's rest in a week from labor is, for man and beast, essential to the best refreshment, the greatest vigor, and longest life.

In requiring men to remember the Sabbath-day to keep it holy, God regards not only his own glory, but the comfort and highest good of all classes of men and of laboring animals.  To deprive them of the rest of the Sabbath is robbery of God, and of man and beast.

entries.title: Exodus 23:13
segments: Circumspect; very careful to obey his will.

entries.title: Exodus 23:15
segments: Feast of unleavened bread; this followed the passover, instituted the night before they left Egypt.  It was called the feast of unleavened bread because they were required, during that feast, to eat nothing leavened, and to have no leaven in their houses.
Empty; without an offering, or something devoted especially to the Lord.

entries.title: Exodus 23:16
segments: Feast of harvest; so called because the harvest then began to be ripe.  It was called also the feast of weeks, or of sevens, because it was kept seven weeks after the passover; also the feast of Pentecost, which means the fiftieth, because it commenced on the fiftieth day after the passover, and was commemorative of the giving of the law from mount Sinai, which took place fifty days after the departure of the Israelites from Egypt.

The feast of ingathering; so called because it took place after the gathering in or completion of the harvest.  It was called also the feast of tabernacles, in commemoration of their having dwelt forty years in tabernacles or tents in the wilderness.  The feast was kept from the fourteenth to the twenty-first day of the month Tishri, answering to the last part of September and the first part of October. It was the seventh month of their ecclesiastical, and the first of their civil year.

entries.title: Exodus 23:17
segments: Not only indidivuals but nations are bound to follow the directions of God.  Nor does their safety or their best interest ever require them, as nations or individuals, to break his commands.

entries.title: Exodus 23:18
segments: The blood of my sacrifice; or the feast of the passover.

entries.title: Exodus 23:19
segments: Seethe; boil or cook.  Some suppose that this precept was intended to guard against a superstitious usage of the heathen; others, that its design was to inculcate a humane spirit.

entries.title: Exodus 23:20
segments: An Angel;he who dwelt in the pillar of cloud and of fire.

entries.title: Exodus 23:21
segments: My name is in him; he possessed and manifested the attributes of Jehovah.

entries.title: Exodus 23:23
segments: Mine Angel shall--bring thee in;

entries.title: Exodus 23:26
segments: Thy days I will fulfil; he would preserve their lives to a good old age.

entries.title: Exodus 23:28
segments: Hornets;

entries.title: Exodus 23:29
segments: Beast of the field; wild and ravenous beasts.

entries.title: Exodus 23:31
segments:
Sea of the Philistines; the Mediterranean sea, on the eastern shore of which the Philistines lived. 
 
  The desert;of Shur. 
 
  The river; Euphrates.
Jehovah claims and exercises the right to dispose of all parts of the earth according to his pleasure.

entries.title: Exodus 23:32
segments: No covenant--with their gods; not worship them.

entries.title: Exodus 23:33
segments: A snare; it would draw them away from the worship of Jehovah, and bring upon them his wrath.
